comparison: Both address cleavage site specificity (C39, C8, C51, C57, C58, C59). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by multiple experimental approaches. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, citing concerns about additional bands at unexpected positions (22nt, 21nt for 33nt substrate; 36nt, 28nt, 13nt for 81nt substrate) and questioning whether cleavage is 'somewhat approximate' at the two sites.

Both evaluate Grc3-dependent activation of Las1 (C46, C47, C48, C33). OpenEval and peer review both find claims SUPPORTED. Peer review also includes C117 and C145 regarding weak Las1 activity alone versus strong activity in complex, confirming the biochemical evidence is convincing.

Both assess structural data quality (C3, C4, C41, C42, C68, C69, C72, C73, C119). OpenEval and peer review both find claims SUPPORTED. Peer review specifically praises the use of both X-ray and cryo-EM approaches and notes significant improvement in structural model quality.

Both evaluate tetrameric assembly and domain organization (C76-C88). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED but cautions about the butterfly analogy, noting the complex has C2 symmetry (180° rotation) rather than mirror symmetry as in real butterflies.

Both address CC domain role in RNA binding and cleavage (C94, C95, C96). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with some speculation about stabilization. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the CC domain is involved in 'only binding RNA or both binding and cleavage,' indicating the precise functional role remains ambiguous.

Both evaluate GCT binding to HEPN active center and Trp617 role (C98, C100-C107). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by structural and mutagenesis data. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED, confirming that structures show C-terminal Grc3 binding to Las1 active pocket and mutation experiments demonstrate importance of these residues.

OpenEval evaluates conserved residues essential for activation (C108, C109) and finds SUPPORTED. Peer review R7 addresses overlapping claims about Grc3-Las1 interaction including these residues, finding them SUPPORTED as part of the broader interaction mechanism.

Both evaluate LCT-CTD interaction (C110-C116). OpenEval and peer review both find claims SUPPORTED. Peer review notes that LCT region in Las1 inserts into Grc3 forming stable complex, and mutations affect activity, strengthening evidence for complex formation.

Both address conformational changes upon Grc3 binding (C131-C138). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by structural comparison showing RMSD values and catalytic pocket changes. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED, noting superposition shows conformational differences and different distances between active site residues explaining activity changes.

Both evaluate species differences in activity (C139, C140, C70, C71). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED, correlating structural differences with activity differences. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED, noting it is interesting that CjGrc3 shows weak activation while ScGrc3 shows strong activation despite structural similarity.

OpenEval evaluates His130 conformational differences (C141, C142) and finds SUPPORTED though somewhat speculative. Peer review R9 addresses broader conformational changes including these claims, finding them SUPPORTED as part of the activation mechanism.

Both evaluate phosphorylation and degradation experiments (C60-C63). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by mobility shift and degradation assays. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED, with no specific concerns raised about these experiments demonstrating 5'-OH termini generation and subsequent processing.

Both evaluate control experiments showing Las1 is responsible for cleavage (C65, C66, C67). OpenEval and peer review both find claims SUPPORTED by controls showing Grc3 alone has no activity, HEPN mutations abolish cleavage, and metal independence.

Both address conserved versus divergent domain conformations (C89, C90). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by structural superposition. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED, noting CC domains have different structures and positions in ScLas1-Grc3 vs CjLas1-Grc3, suggesting they are more dynamic.

OpenEval evaluates CC domain composition and lack of homologs (C91, C92, C93) and finds SUPPORTED. Peer review R5 addresses CC domain structural differences (C92, C93) as part of broader comparison, finding them SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates specific cleavage sites and product sizes (C49, C50, C52, C53, C55) and finds SUPPORTED. Peer review R1 addresses these claims as part of broader cleavage site evaluation but rates UNCERTAIN due to additional unexpected bands.

OpenEval evaluates sequential cleavage and 23-nt intermediate (C54, C56) and finds SUPPORTED. Peer review R1 addresses these as part of cleavage mechanism but rates UNCERTAIN, noting mass spec shows intermediate products that may indicate two binding events rather than single binding.

Both evaluate the proposed processing pathway (C147, C148, C149, C150, C151). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED and well-integrated with literature. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, questioning whether both C2 and C2' cleavage occur in single binding event or require multiple binding events, citing intermediate products in mass spec.

OpenEval evaluates RNA structure model for sequential cleavage (C155, C156, C157) and rates UNCERTAIN, noting it lacks direct experimental validation. Peer review R12 addresses the broader mechanism including this model, also rating UNCERTAIN and questioning single versus multiple binding events.

OpenEval evaluates functional organization of active centers (C152, C153, C154) and finds SUPPORTED though functional independence not directly tested. Peer review R12 addresses broader mechanism including these claims, rating UNCERTAIN due to questions about binding events.

OpenEval evaluates HEPN dimer instability and Grc3 stabilization (C145, C146, C117, C118) and finds SUPPORTED. Peer review R2 addresses C117 and C145 as part of Grc3-dependent activation, finding them SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates CjLas1 HEPN crystal structure and monomer-dimer equilibrium (C120-C130) and finds claims SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific structural claims about the isolated HEPN domain.
OpenEval evaluates use of cryo-EM maps for molecular replacement (C74, C75) and finds SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological claims.
OpenEval evaluates claim that P3 length limits degradation (C64) and rates UNCERTAIN, noting speculation without direct testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.

OpenEval evaluates novel activation mechanism compared to other HEPN nucleases (C158-C167) and finds SUPPORTED by structural data and literature comparison. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these comparative mechanism claims.

OpenEval evaluates comparison with Ire1 and RNase L systems (C168-C178) and finds SUPPORTED by structural comparison and literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these broader comparative claims.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about ribosome biosynthesis and pre-rRNA processing (C1, C10-C38, C43-C45, C143-C144) and finds SUPPORTED by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as these are contextual background claims.
